leftEvidence.title: Satan masquerades as an angel of light through deceptive appearance

points.label: Appearance and naming
points.left: Satan masquerades as an angel of light through deceptive appearance
points.right: The source names Satan as the dragon, serpent, deceiver, and accuser.

points.label: Associated agents
points.left: Paul speaks of jealousy, another Jesus, a different spirit, and a different message of good news. He names deceitful workers who disguise themselves. Satan also disguises himself as an angel of light, and his servants pose as servants of righteousness. Their end will match their works.
points.right: A woman gives birth while a dragon waits. Her child is taken to God’s throne, and she flees into the wilderness. Michael and his angels fight the dragon and cast him out. The source names him as the old serpent, devil, Satan, deceiver, and accuser. Victory, a short time, pursuit, protection, a flood, the earth, and the woman’s offspring complete the vision.

payload.posture: Read both WEBU passages side by side. Keep each passage’s actors, setting, order, and identity claims distinct.

rightEvidence.title: The source names Satan as the dragon, serpent, deceiver, and accuser.

payload.tension: One source shows Satan hiding behind a good appearance. The other openly names the dragon, serpent, deceiver, and accuser.
payload.title: An angel-of-light disguise and an openly named dragon
